title: From Disengaged to Selective: The Profiles of Young Adult Daters
author: Alan J. Hawkins et al.
summary: Alan Hawkins, Jason Carroll, Brian Willoughby and Anna Elmer extend earlier Wheatley Institute findings of a dating recession among young adults. Using the 2025 National Dating Landscape Survey, they argue that a single statistic hides diversity and identify three dater profiles: unprepared, selective and active. Unprepared daters, about 37 percent, date rarely, have low confidence and fewer resources, and are less religious. Selective daters, about 45 percent and mostly educated women, date infrequently but seriously and want marriage soon. Active daters, about 18 percent and mostly men, date the most but avoid serious commitment despite valuing marriage, and report heavy pornography and AI companion use. The authors conclude that the groups are equally dissatisfied with their options and need different help: skills and low-cost options, dating pathways, and resilience around past breakups.
points: The dating recession is not uniform: low-frequency dating hides two very different groups, the unprepared and the selective.
Unprepared daters lack confidence, money and parental support, so parents and educators can help most by building dating skills and surfacing low-cost options.
Selective daters are confident and serious and appear to need dating pathways that match their intent more than dating education.
Active daters date for social reasons and fear commitment, partly because of painful past breakups, so they need resilience and help examining their fears.
All three groups are equally dissatisfied with their dating options, and money was the most endorsed barrier to dating in the survey.
quotes: Specifically, we found that less than a third of young adults in the prime serious dating years (ages 22-35)—who expect to marry in the future—are dating at least once a month.
Simply put, it is not very helpful to see all young adults through a single statistic of central tendency.
Interestingly, the three groups are equally dissatisfied with their dating options (although their “meh” feelings might come from different experiences).
Selective Daters—the other low-frequency-dating group, and the largest group overall—have much higher confidence in their dating skills.
Young adults who are dating the most do so for social reasons and have fears of serious relationships and commitment, even though marriage is important and salient to them.
This group, it seems, needs more help finding dating partners who match their serious orientation to dating. They need dating pathways more than dating education.
